subject: ApexBridge on‑prem readiness: node grid, storage acceptance, and network gating
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@apexbridge.com>

Subject: Initial site details and ask for on‑prem plan

Hiro —

Thanks again for the pre‑sales call today. Attached is our simplified inventory and a rough network diagram for the DC on Floor 2. We want Redwood Private in a VPC‑like, air‑gapped topology inside our cage; main constraints below: 

- 3 racks (A/B/C) with mixed GPU and storage nodes.
- Strict outbound egress via a NAT pair; only a few management IPs allowed.
- Storage: two tiers — local NVMe for ephemeral KV caches and a HA blockstore (iSCSI/Ceph) for persistent volumes.
- Compliance: we need an audit trail and KMS integration (we can provide HSM details later).

Can you draft a short nodepool + storage acceptance plan (what we should provision, storage classes, eviction policies, basic network gating rules) and identify open questions we should answer before we sign the Dedicated contract?

I attached: apexbridge-inventory-20270314.csv and site-network-diagram-APX-floor2.pdf

Looking for a brief writeup and a 30‑minute technical walkthrough early next week.

Subject: Re: Initial site details and ask for on‑prem plan

Oliver —

Appreciate the inventory + diagram. I put together a concise acceptance plan below for the on‑prem cluster (high level so the ops/arch folks can confirm):

1) Cluster footprint and nodepools
- Control plane: 3 x m48‑class control VMs (non‑GPU), dedicated management network, with etcd pinned to local NVMe and snapshot replication to the blockstore.
- Inference GPU pool: 4 x p4/p40 equivalent nodes per rack (scale target: 8–12k token/s for baseline model). GPU nodepool should expose a local NVMe for KV cache (ephemeral) + ephemeral scratch.
- Worker pool (stateless preprocessors): mix of CPU‑optimized nodes, autoscaling based on queue depth.
- Storage gateway (stateful): 3 replicas of large memory/cpu nodes that mount the HA blockstore (iSCSI/Ceph), host CSI controllers, and expose PVs.

2) Storage classes and policies
- sc‑nvme‑ephemeral (LocalStorage) — for KV cache and latency‑sensitive runtime cache, node affinity to GPU nodes, no replication (rely on request replay).
- sc‑blockstore‑fast (ReadWriteOnce/Provisioned iSCSI) — for model artifacts and persistent DBs; multipath + periodic snapshots to external backup target.
- sc‑archive (ReadWriteMany via CephFS or NFS) — for logs, long‑term artifacts; enforce retention policy.
- Eviction/QoS: GPU nodes should reserve a headroom token (10% CPU and memory) and use podPriority for graceful eviction of non‑critical workloads.

3) Networking and gating (open questions below)
- Management network separate from inference egress; only management VLAN allowed to reach Redwood control plane endpoints.
- Egress: list of allowed destinations (redwood update endpoints, metrics, and KMS) — need ApexBridge to provide appliance IPs that can talk outbound.
- NAT and anti‑spoofing: ensure SNAT for egress is via dedicated NAT pair; avoid floating IPs on worker interface.

4) Observability / audit
- Enable token‑level request logging (audit trail) and forward to your SIEM via secure syslog to the aggregator on the archive network.
- Integrate KMS: Redwood will use your KMS HSM endpoint for envelope keys; need endpoint + CA cert.

Open questions we need answered before final acceptance plan:
- Can the blockstore present iSCSI LUNs with multipath to the three storage gateway nodes?
- Which IP ranges are allowed for outbound (for updates/metrics)?
- Do you require air‑gapped install (no outbound) or restricted outbound to specific endpoints?
- Backup target: do you have an internal S3 compatible endpoint or do we use the blockstore snapshots?

Proposed next steps: 30‑minute tech walkthrough Wednesday 2027‑03‑17 09:00–09:30 PT. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short pre‑read with the high‑level network ACLs we’ll propose.

Irene and Marissa from my team are cc’d — Irene will validate network gating and Marissa will own runbook/ops handoff items.

Thanks —

Oliver / Hiro —

Quick network checklist and gating constraints from our side (I reviewed the attached diagram):

- VLANs: recommend a three‑VLAN split per rack: mgmt (VLAN 10), infra (VLAN 20), tenant/compute (VLAN 30). Keep control nodes on mgmt only.
- BGP/Edge: If you have a top‑of‑rack BGP speaker, we prefer to peer for transit with a /29 for the NAT pair. Otherwise we will rely on your firewall NAT rules.
- Egress ACLs (required):
  - redwood-control.redwood.example.com:443
  - metrics.redwood.example.com:443 (for telemetry)
  - kms.apexbridge.local:443
  - ntp.pool.org:123 (or your internal NTP)

- Port mapping for CSI & iSCSI: 3260 inbound from storage gateway nodes to blockstore; ensure iscsi CHAP credentials are available.
- MTU: set 9000 across infra/compute VLANs to avoid fragmentation for model artifacts.

Open items for ApexBridge to confirm:
1) CHAP creds and whether iSCSI LUNs support multipath.
2) Can you provide a management jump host reachable from Redwood ops for initial bootstrap (we prefer a bastion with limited window access)?
3) Your air‑gap policy: if complete offline, we will need an offline installer image and separate license server.

I’ll prepare recommended ACL snippets and a small diagram overlay for the pre‑read.

—Irene
